units.source: Search

Note search enables you to find notes by searching for text in the title, content, or __TRILIUM_PH_0__attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the notes. You also have the option to save your searches, which will create a special search note which is visible on your navigation tree and contains the search results as sub-items.
Types of search__TRILIUM_PH_0__
There are multiple types of searches, all using the same search mechanism and query language:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which can be found in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for small one-off searches.
The results are shown in a popup and it has an infinite scroll.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Full search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the more advanced search mechanism.
The results are displayed in a separate page and it has multiple advanced features (search script, fast search, include archived notes, order by, limit).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Bulk Actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as adding a label/relation can be applied to the results.
The results are paginated and they can be displayed in any __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view (e.g. grid, list, calendar, table).
Some __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as board view have a dedicated search bar which applies to that collection.
In this case, the results are displayed directly in the collection instead of a popup and they are limited to the collection but the query language remains the same.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a similar concept but it's mainly used to search for notes by title, not by content. Nevertheless, it also features a way to search in full text if the results are unsatisfactory.
Accessing the search__TRILIUM_PH_0__
From the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, look for the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_2__ search button.

To limit the search to a note and its children, select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search in subtree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note tree contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ or press __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_6__+__TRILIUM_PH_7__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_8__+__TRILIUM_PH_9__S__TRILIUM_PH_10__.

Go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to & command palette__TRILIUM_PH_1__, look for something then press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show in full search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ below the results (or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_7__).
Interaction__TRILIUM_PH_0__
To search for notes, click on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or press the keyboard __TRILIUM_PH_3__shortcut__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
Set the text to search for in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search string__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field.
Apart from searching for words literally, there is also the possibility to search for attributes or properties of notes.
See the examples below for more information.
To limit the search to a note and its sub-children, set a note in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ancestor__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
This value is also pre-filled if the search is triggered from a __TRILIUM_PH_0__hoisted note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or a __TRILIUM_PH_2__workspace__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
To search the entire database, keep the value empty.

To limit the search to only a few levels of hierarchy (e.g. look in sub-children but not in sub-sub-children of a note), set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__depth__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field to one of the provided values.
In addition to that, the search can be configured via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add search option__TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu, as described in the follow-up section.
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) to trigger the search. The results are displayed below the search configuration pane.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search & Execute actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) entry in the menu beside __TRILIUM_PH_3__Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__ is only relevant if at least one action has been added (as described in the section below).

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save to note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) entry in the same menu will create a new note with the search configuration. For more information, see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
Features__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Autocomplete__TRILIUM_PH_0__
To help with the syntax, Trilium offers an autocomplete functionality which can be triggered by pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Some suggestions also open on their own as you type: label and relation names after __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__, fields after __TRILIUM_PH_2__, operators, values, and notes after __TRILIUM_PH_3__. Keywords such as __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__, __TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__ appear only on __TRILIUM_PH_9__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_10__+__TRILIUM_PH_11__Space__TRILIUM_PH_12__, since a plain word is usually a search term.

No suggestion is selected when a list opens on its own, so __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ runs the search as typed. To insert a suggestion, select it with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Down__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and press __TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__. The list opened with __TRILIUM_PH_6__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_7__+__TRILIUM_PH_8__Space__TRILIUM_PH_9__ and the notes after __TRILIUM_PH_10__ open on the best match instead, so __TRILIUM_PH_11__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_12__ inserts it.
The autocomplete offers:
Basic operators such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and keywords (__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__).
Fields for object-like fields such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__, triggered by typing __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
Contextual enumerations such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ names by typing __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
A small gear on the name's icon indicates a system attribute.
After typing the label name, the value is also autocompleted with values that are present in the database.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Relation__TRILIUM_PH_1__ names by typing __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Note ID__TRILIUM_PH_1__s can be inserted easily by typing __TRILIUM_PH_2__ and looking for a note.
If the note ID is under a valid syntax, it will be shown as a chip of the note instead of the raw ID.
This is especially useful for queries that make use of the note ID such as searching by template: __TRILIUM_PH_0__
Syntax highlighting__TRILIUM_PH_0__
The search input features syntax highlighting, making recognized fields such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and operators like __TRILIUM_PH_1__ stand out.

The same highlighting is available in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, for example to keep a collection of queries: set the language of the note to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Trilium Search Query__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The language is not enabled by default; add it from __TRILIUM_PH_4__Options__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Code Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__ → __TRILIUM_PH_8__Available MIME types in the dropdown__TRILIUM_PH_9__.
Error highlighting & linting__TRILIUM_PH_0__
The search is also checked for errors in two phases, which will be displayed as a red squiggle:
Linter errors which identify common error patterns and also provide a way to fix them.
Search errors which are checked by the server, without indicating the exact place the error occurred.

An error the search only runs into while running, such as an operator that note content cannot be searched with, is shown in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search error__TRILIUM_PH_1__ card instead: below the search string, or at the top of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Quick search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ results.
Multiline__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Long or complicated searches can be formatted by using newlines, similar to SQL queries. Newlines are treated just like spaces.
To add a new line, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Multiline is available only for the full search, other inputs such as the quick search or the collection filter are single line.
Search options__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Click __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add search option__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to choose an option to apply.
For each search option selected, the search configuration will update to reveal the entry. Each search option will have its own configuration.
To remove a search option, simply press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to the right of it.
The options available are:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Search script
This feature allows writing a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note that will handle the search on its own.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Fast search
The search will not look into the content of the notes, but it will still look into note titles and attributes, relations (based on the search query).
This method can speed up the search considerably for large __TRILIUM_PH_0__databases__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Include archived
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Archived Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will also be included in the results, whereas otherwise they would be ignored.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Order by
Allows changing the criteria for ordering the results, for example to order by creation date or alphabetically instead of by relevancy (default).
It's also possible to change the order (ascending or descending) of the results.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Limit
Limits the results to a given maximum.
This can help if the number of results would otherwise be high, at the cost of not being able to view all the results.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Debug
This will print additional information in the server log (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Error logs__TRILIUM_PH_1__), regarding how the search expression was parsed.
This function is especially useful after understanding the search functionality in detail, in order to determine why a complex search query is not working as expected.

The same menu ends with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Bulk actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section for applying changes such as adding a label or a relation to the matched notes. Its groups—__TRILIUM_PH_2__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Other__TRILIUM_PH_9__—each open a list of the actions in the corresponding group of the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Bulk Actions__TRILIUM_PH_11__ dialog, which is an alternative for operating directly with notes within the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_13__. Choosing one adds it to the search; unlike the other options, the same action can be added more than once (e.g. to apply multiple labels). After defining the actions, first press __TRILIUM_PH_14__Search__TRILIUM_PH_15__ to check the matched notes and then choose __TRILIUM_PH_16__Search & Execute actions__TRILIUM_PH_17__ from the menu beside it to trigger the actions.
Viewing search results__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Results appear below the search pane, by default in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view. Each result is drawn as a __TRILIUM_PH_2__snippet card__TRILIUM_PH_3__ with the note title, the path to it, a short excerpt of the matching text, and the attributes that matched. The excerpt of a code note keeps its indentation and is shown in the code font.

To show the results as a plain note list instead, choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__List__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_3__ bar. The __TRILIUM_PH_4__List__TRILIUM_PH_5__ view shows one row per note, with the note's title and content preview.
The search will also highlight the words from the title or content that matched:
With a solid underlined green for a direct match;
With a dotted underline orange for a partial match (matched by the fuzzy search).
In addition, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view offers:
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__total number of results__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is always shown, so you can immediately tell how broad a query is.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__page-size selector__TRILIUM_PH_1__ lets you choose how many results to display per page. Your choice is remembered and synced across your devices (stored in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ option), so you do not have to reset it on every device.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Clicking a result's title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ opens the note and jumps straight to the first match. The in-note find bar opens pre-filled with the first word of your search, so you can step through its matches with the find controls. To have the find bar look for a whole phrase instead, put the phrase in quotes in the search, e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_2__. In read-only notes, the other words of the search are highlighted as well. The excerpt and attributes can be selected without opening the note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Open all results in new tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__, the button above the results) opens every result in a tab of its own, up to 50. Each tab opens on its first match with the find bar pre-filled, as when clicking a result.
If a match is inside a __TRILIUM_PH_0__collapsed section__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (for example a folded heading), that section is expanded automatically so the match is visible.

When the excerpt is cut short, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show more__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button expands the card to the note's full content, with the search terms highlighted. __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show less__TRILIUM_PH_3__ returns to the excerpt.

A saved search can also be __TRILIUM_PH_0__printed or exported as PDF__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Print/export to PDF…__TRILIUM_PH_3__ item of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_5__, in either __TRILIUM_PH_6__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_7__ or __TRILIUM_PH_8__List__TRILIUM_PH_9__ view. The results are laid out as a list, as they stand when printing starts.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__: Use boolean expressions and parentheses to group expressions.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__: A group can open the expression part directly, without a __TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__ before the parenthesis. Here it finds notes containing "towers" whose genre is fantasy or scifi.

A link is a relation you created, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, or one that content creates: an internal link (__TRILIUM_PH_1__), an image (__TRILIUM_PH_2__), an included note (__TRILIUM_PH_3__) or a relation map connection (__TRILIUM_PH_4__). Relations that configure a note, such as __TRILIUM_PH_5__ or a saved search's __TRILIUM_PH_6__, are not links.
See also __TRILIUM_PH_0__Under the hood__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for more syntax references.
